items.title: Rust costs the world about 3 percent of global GDP every year
items.claim: The NACE International IMPACT study (2016) estimated the global cost of corrosion at 2.5 trillion US dollars per year — about 3.4 percent of global GDP. Bridges, ships, pipelines, vehicles, buildings: the world fights iron's tendency to oxidise.
items.prompt: What makes iron-based rust particularly destructive?

options.text: Iron oxide (Fe2O3) has greater volume than the iron it formed from, so it flakes off rather than forming a protective layer; underlying metal is constantly exposed, and the process continues until the structure fails
Iron rusts in a chain reaction

items.reveal:
When aluminium oxidises, Al2O3 has nearly the same molar volume as the metal, forming a tight, protective coating. When iron oxidises, hydrated Fe2O3 occupies more space than the metal, breaks free, flakes off, and exposes fresh iron to the next round.

The Pilling-Bedworth ratio for iron is about 2.1 (oxide volume vs metal volume). For aluminium it's about 1.3. A ratio close to 1 gives a protective layer; ratios much larger than 1 give flaking; ratios much smaller than 1 give porous, useless layers.

Protection strategies: galvanising (zinc sacrificial anode), painting (barrier coating), stainless-steel alloying with Cr (which forms protective Cr2O3), cathodic protection (applied voltage), and design choices to keep moisture off.
items.why: Rust is taught as 'iron + oxygen + water'. The economics and the engineering of corrosion control are vast.

items.title: The same element you breathe shields the planet from UV
items.claim: Atmospheric oxygen is O2 — diatomic, vital for respiration. Ozone is O3 — pale blue, pungent, toxic at ground level and protective at altitude. Same element, two molecules, opposite roles.
items.prompt: Why does ozone behave so differently from O2?

options.text: O3's bent three-atom structure with delocalised pi bonding absorbs strongly in the 200-310 nm UV range; O2's MO structure has no comparable visible or near-UV absorption
O3 contains an extra proton per atom

items.reveal:
Ozone is bent with O-O-O angle about 117 degrees and two resonance structures. Its electronic transitions absorb the biologically damaging Hartley UV band.

The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs to protect the stratospheric ozone layer. It is the most successful environmental treaty by measurable atmospheric impact. The ozone layer is now slowly recovering.

Ground-level ozone produced by photochemical smog damages lungs at parts-per-billion concentrations. Same molecule, life-saving at 30 km, lung-damaging at the surface.
items.why: Allotropes aren't just minor structural variants — they can be biologically and atmospherically opposite.
